verses.pali: Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: Seated to one side, that mendicant said to the Buddha:

verses.pali: “ko nu kho, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo, yenekadā uṇhaṁ hotī”ti?
verses.english: “Sir, what is the cause, what is the reason why sometimes it becomes warm?”
“Mendicant, there are what are called gods of the warm thunderclouds.

verses.pali: ‘yannūna mayaṁ sakāya ratiyā vaseyyāmā’ti, tesaṁ taṁ cetopaṇidhimanvāya uṇhaṁ hoti.
verses.english: ‘Why don’t we revel in our own kind of enjoyment?’ Then, in accordance with their wish, it becomes warm.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ kho, bhikkhu, hetu, ayaṁ paccayo, yenekadā uṇhaṁ hotī”ti.
verses.english: This is the cause, this is the reason why sometimes it becomes warm.”
